Elastic Constants: E, ν, λ, μ
section: What do λ and μ mean physically?
text:
What do λ and μ mean physically?
\(\mu\) resists pure shape change (shear). \(\lambda\) is subtler — it’s the stress that appears sideways only when lateral strain is prevented (confined loading), not something you’d feel in a free pull test.

title: Deviatoric / Spherical Decomposition
text:
Any strain (or stress) tensor splits into a volumetric (spherical) part — pure isotropic scaling, no shape change — and a deviatoric part — pure shape change, no volume change:
\[
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon} = \underbrace{\varepsilon_v\mathbf{I}}_{\text{spherical}} + \underbrace{(\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}-\varepsilon_v\mathbf{I})}_{\text{deviatoric}}, \qquad \varepsilon_v = \frac{1}{3}\text{tr}(\boldsymbol{\varepsilon})
\]
Drag the sliders below to set \(\varepsilon_{11},\varepsilon_{22},\varepsilon_{12}\) and watch the volumetric part stay square while the deviatoric part distorts at constant area.

title: Stress & Strain: The 1D Picture
text:
A typical uniaxial stress-strain response shows a linear elastic region up to a yield point, followed by strain hardening to the ultimate tensile strength (UTS), then softening (necking) to fracture.

Note: this is a schematic, not-to-scale illustration — real elastic strains are far smaller relative to the plastic strain range than shown here.

title: Yield Criteria: Von Mises vs Tresca
text:
\[
\sigma_{VM} = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2}\left[(\sigma_1-\sigma_2)^2+(\sigma_2-\sigma_3)^2+(\sigma_3-\sigma_1)^2\right]}
\]
\[
\sigma_{Tresca} = \sigma_{max}-\sigma_{min}
\]
Both are pressure-independent — motion purely along the hydrostatic axis (\(\sigma_1=\sigma_2=\sigma_3\)) never triggers yield under either criterion. Projected onto the π-plane, Von Mises is a circle and Tresca is a hexagon inscribed inside it, touching exactly at the uniaxial-stress corners.

The two criteria always agree at the hexagon’s corners and diverge most at the edge midpoints (pure-shear states), where Tresca is more conservative by \(2/\sqrt{3}\approx1.155\).
